text:
I just recently (early January 2019) purchased Fallout 76 at $20 off for PC at Walmart. First of all, the "physical copy" is just a cardboard cutout with a download code where a Blu-ray or DVD would usually sit. I knew this ahead of time, but as an FYI, if you're looking to not have such a big download, there's no way around it.
After several hours, the game just isn't much fun. The new world is refreshing because Fallout is normally drab looking and samey after a while. Its charm wears out quicker than you'd expect.
- Load times are not great
- Lag is very prevalent in enemies and it sometimes makes them difficult to hit unless using V.A.T.S.
- Since starting S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats are 1's all around, you'll find it difficult to carry much and I found myself hugging a circle around stash boxes and workbenches to keep breaking down and storing junk
- I disliked terminals and holotapes in Fallout 4, and that's most of what there is in the way of questing for Fallout 76 since there are no living human NPCs
- They took some good from Fallout 3 and some good from Fallout 4 and mixed it together, while simultaneously changing both to make mechanics less fun (ie. weapon/armor durability, modification, weapon levels, etc.)
- Favorites and d-pad mappings were modified and made much less effective compared to Fallout 4
- I don't understand where they were going with the social aspects. I've played WoW, Age of Conan, Darkfall Online, etc. and I know Bethesda is new to online games, but just having multiple players in any previous fallout game without additional features would have been fantastic. Changes they made just for the multiplayer don't feel right
I find myself wishing I'd saved my $40 and just installed a couple Fallout 4 mods. Maybe a seasons mod with spring to add some color like 76 and a couple quest line mods to add a bit more content. It's not just a bunch of salty fanboys wanting a proper Fallout game that are giving this a low rating - it's just not that fun. As a fan of Bethesda games from Morrowind through Fallout 4, I just can't endorse Fallout 76. Maybe if you snag it for only $20 total, but even then I can't imagine spending a whole lot of time on the game.

text:
No one wanted see this game succeed more than me. I love the fallout series and was super stoked to make some new friends to go around and punch radiated stuff in the face with.
None of that has really happened.
First off, EVERY TIME they patch it makes a few things better and other things worse. Whenever they do big patches it really kills the stability of the game or the server.
Part of the game is already ruined beyond belief. It took them so long to fix the item duping people were doing that the damage is already done. There are cheaters who carry hundreds of items that no one would ever be able to collect hundreds of and they hurt server and any economic stability.
The end game is a massive joke. When you can manage to get a nuke launched without getting dc'd or crashing (which also makes you start the entire process over) you roll the dice on crashing half way through the fight or finishing the fight and the scrochbeast queen dropping literally the worst trash legendary you've ever seen.
As far as quests go there's hardly any. The events are repeatable but most of them are mind numbingly dull at a higher level and even the ones that can be difficult (AWOL armaments and One violent night) are kind of a toss up on how many things actually spawn. (I once killed a whole 6 feral ghouls for the entire one violent night event)
It has also become increasingly clear that Bethesda gives at least about the same amount of effort in making reskins to sell in their micro-transaction store as they do actually fixing the game.
Items are woefully imbalanced as well. Unless you lucked out and bought a duped double shot explosive round gun or was one of the few people to actually get one, you're pretty much a fairly low DPS character.
The loot tables for rare mobs and legendaries is even more laughable. Most of the legendary drops are completely useless in the game and would never, ever, ever, ever be used by any player in the right mind. A pole cue that does 30% more damage to super mutants?! HUZAAAHHHHH SO USEFUL ¬_¬
I decided to wait two months before leaving a review on this game because Bethesda is notorious for putting out garbage day one and making it gold after a couple of months. Fallout 76 is the exception.
Literally every move forward has an accompanied move or two backwards.
If you are curious about this game I urge you, wait until it only costs $10. Which at the rate things are going, should only be a few months.
If you love fallout avoid this game at all cost. It's the worst in the series by very large margin.

text:
So I will start by openly saying I love this throwback series of 2D side scrolling super Mario bros. While I had this on the Wii U along with the included Luigi aka time
Trial version I actually never got the chance to
Finish it. Having the chance to be able to play this on the go is fantastic and gives you a nice dose of modernized Mario nostalgia. This is also another really good game that kids can play who are newer to gaming and platformers. I will say that if you played through New Super Mario Bros U and/or New Luigi U and are hoping for something new you may be disappointed and find it better to
Wait for a price drop or skip the game entirely. There isn't much added besides some slightly improved resolution and the ability to play Toadette. Toadette actually is a great character for newer / inexperienced players to play with and has the fun ability to actually transform into Peachette with the crown powerup. New Luigi U is still fun but is really more of a time rush game taking place in similar worlds. I think this game is fun but it would be nice if Nintendo rereleased this game without the infamous "Switch tax" for a lower price. I know it's a first party Nintendo game so a price reduction is unlikely but I do feel like given the age of this rerelease (6 years?) a price point of around $29.99 would have truly been perfect despite many fans likely missing out the Wii U version due to its poor sales.

text:
If you are familiar with Skylanders, Starlink is no different. You get a mount that clips onto your controller. Onto the mount you clip a pilot, then a ship, then ship accessories (weapons). The mount senses what is clipped on and the game changes based on what you have equipped.

First things - the mount is wired. It connects to your console, but does have a pretty long cord. The base set comes with one pilot, one ship, and three weapons. You can have only two weapons equipped at one time on the base ship, so you get to choose among weapons a bit, but that is the only choice available without buying more toys.

The mount took a second to figure out at first as it is not as simple as the "stage" used with Skylander figurines. It works well and did not in the way of gameplay while I was using it. Every weapon change I did happened exactly as expected and was done quickly. Weapons not only have different 'types' that can be more or less effective depending on your enemy/environment. In other similar games, some character and/or add-on figures have exhaustion, forcing you to change them out after a certain amount of gameplay. I did not encounter that with Starlink.

My understanding is that you can buy all the add-ons in digital form or physical form. The digital form would allow for gameplay without the controller mount and physical toys. I have not tried that, but it is appealing.

Clearly I am not super excited about the toys.

What about the video game itself? Well, I have not finished it, but I have enjoyed the worlds I have played. They are dynamic, good looking, and fun to explore. I have not experienced the type of wonder while exploring as I have with some other open world games, but this is much more of a flying game than an RPG really.

What does that mean to gameplay? Well, you are always flying. In space, the battlefield is 3D, the controls were fine, and I was able to keep in the battle (I'm not normally a flight sim/dog fight type of player). On the ground you are still in your ship, and still flying, but everything is mostly 2D. What I mean is that you can't usually gain altitude to deal with a situation, you kind of hover a few ship heights off the ground for the most part.

I love the worlds I have played, though. Varied with interesting plants and geography. I've not gotten too far, but I've been pleased with what I've seen thus far.

Every weapon change I did happened exactly as expected and was done quickly. Weapons not only have different 'types' that can be more or less effective depending on your enemy/environment. In other similar games, some character and/or add-on figures have exhaustion, forcing you to change them out after a certain amount of gameplay. I did not encounter that with Starlink.

My understanding is that you can buy all the add-ons in digital form or physical form. The digital form would allow for gameplay without the controller mount and physical toys. I have not tried that, but it is appealing.

Clearly I am not super excited about the toys.

What about the video game itself? Well, I have not finished it, but I have enjoyed the worlds I have played. They are dynamic, good looking, and fun to explore. I have not experienced the type of wonder while exploring as I have with some other open world games, but this is much more of a flying game than an RPG really.

What does that mean to gameplay? Well, you are always flying. In space, the battlefield is 3D, the controls were fine, and I was able to keep in the battle (I'm not normally a flight sim/dog fight type of player). On the ground you are still in your ship, and still flying, but everything is mostly 2D. What I mean is that you can't usually gain altitude to deal with a situation, you kind of hover a few ship heights off the ground for the most part.

I love the worlds I have played, though. Varied with interesting plants and geography. I've not gotten too far, but I've been pleased with what I've seen thus far.

text:
Final Fantasy 12 has been one of my favorite games for years. I got it brand new for the PlayStation 2 back in 2006 and I have put in well over 900 hours into the game over the years. I still play on the PS2 version, and I wanted to try out the remaster of this game since I had heard really good things about it. And I must say that I love this game, but oh do I love the 4x speed option. It makes the grinding and the farming of items and weapons in the first few hours of the game SOOOOOOOO much easier. I love being OP as F***, because I did struggle the first 2-3 times I played this game, and as such, I can spend just a few hours chaining Dustia in the Westersand to raise my level by 30 before I even get a second character.
Having the option to get the voices in the original Japanese as well makes it much easier to actually get back into the storyline as well. I don't know why, but the 3 most prevalent characters, (namely Vaan, Penelo, and Ashe), their voice acting at the beginning of the game makes my ears bleed. I still love the characters and the storyline, it's just those characters voices that annoy me. Being able to turn off the subtitles allows me to practice my Japanese, and being able to change the other options, such as battle speed, on the fly makes this game fresh again. I'm loving the game and I really hope more people get into this game. Be it a revisit to an old friend or a new adventure I wish all players luck.
